title: Mixer signed capability grant protocol v2

canonicalization.map_order: bytewise lexicographic order of encoded keys
canonicalization.data_model: text keys and values, unsigned integers, arrays, maps and booleans; all declared struct fields included, no nulls or omitted fields
canonicalization.artifact_signature: Ed25519(mixer.artifact.v2 followed by one NUL byte followed by canonical CBOR manifest)
canonicalization.assignment_signature: Ed25519(mixer.assignment.v2 followed by one NUL byte followed by canonical CBOR assignment)
canonicalization.artifact_identity: lowercase SHA256 hex of canonical CBOR manifest
canonicalization.signature_transport: RFC4648 canonical padded standard base64 text encoding exactly 64 bytes; numeric arrays, CR/LF, nonzero pad bits and missing padding reject

negotiation: Installed host protocol exactly 2; manifest schema/protocol exactly 2; assignment schema exactly 2. Protocol1 remains strict release-v1 with v1 signature domains and rejects grants. No implicit upgrade or downgrade. Guest ABI and UI schema remain 1.

manifest_fields.runtime: 64 lowercase hex exact installed runtime fingerprint
manifest_fields.capability_hashes: map identifier to 64 lowercase hex, exact host map match
manifest_fields.expanded_bytes: uint64 identical to compressed_bytes in v2
manifest_fields.asset_hashes: empty map only; separate assets fail closed until verified extraction exists
manifest_fields.source_map_sha256: 64 lowercase hex reference; source map is not executed or fetched by v1
manifest_fields.created_at_unix: positive uint64 audit time, not replay authority

capability_grants.entries: 0..2 closed grant entries; every array explicit, strictly sorted unique ASCII, and every present entry binds its signed capability_hashes schema hash

assignment_fields.sequence: positive uint64 monotonically increasing within app/environment/platform/runtime/channel

capability_grant_descriptor.entry_order: strict ascending ASCII capability_id; reject duplicates
capability_grant_descriptor.set_order: strict ascending ASCII strings; reject duplicates before set conversion
capability_grant_descriptor.missing_entry: deny; installed schema hash alone grants no authority
capability_grant_descriptor.binding: each present entry equals its signed capability_hashes entry and the known schema hash

origins.host_rule: lowercase DNS labels a-z 0-9 hyphen; nonempty labels; no leading or trailing hyphen
origins.port_rule: absent or canonical decimal 1..65535 excluding 443; no leading zeros

storage.keyValue.v1.namespace_rule: case-sensitive ASCII A-Z a-z 0-9 underscore hyphen; length 1..64

capability_grant_descriptor_hash: lowercase SHA256 of RFC8949 core deterministic CBOR of capability_grant_descriptor; bytewise encoded-key ordering; descriptor hash excludes this parent document

capability_grant_entry_fields.capability_id: known capability identifier, unique entry strictly sorted by ASCII
capability_grant_entry_fields.schema_sha256: exact known schema hash and matching signed capability_hashes entry
capability_grant_entry_fields.permissions: explicit strictly sorted unique ASCII array; empty denies; subset of the family permission
capability_grant_entry_fields.origins: explicit strictly sorted unique ASCII array; HTTP exact canonical origins only; empty denies HTTP
capability_grant_entry_fields.methods: explicit strictly sorted unique ASCII array; HTTP allowed method names only; empty denies HTTP
capability_grant_entry_fields.namespaces: explicit strictly sorted unique ASCII array; storage exact identifiers only; empty denies storage

authority: Only successfully signature/payload-verified manifests expose trusted grant data and resource limits. Installed permissions/origins/methods/namespaces intersect the signed grants independently per capability. Missing/empty grants deny; capability_hashes prove compatibility only. Public configuration/model constructors, unverified manifests, sidecars and tool receipts do not confer execution authority.
native_fingerprint: Installed runtime fingerprint must additionally cover installed grants/configuration, generated bridge and native implementation, compiler/toolchain/platform, dependencies, permissions and custom HTTP implementation. This protocol does not generate or attest that fingerprint.
identifier: 1..128 ASCII letters, numbers, dot, underscore or hyphen
cohort: SHA256 of canonical CBOR map {organization,project,app,environment,channel,installation}; treat digest as unsigned big-endian integer modulo 10000; eligible if less than signed rollout_basis_points. Stable expansion; installation ID is app-private random pseudonym, never account/customer data. Reinstallation generates new ID; account switching retains ID.
trust: Direct Ed25519 roots pinned in host/config, exact signed scope, independent artifact/assignment roles, explicit revocation and optional not-before/not-after. No delegation documents supported; unknown protocol features reject. Rotation needs preinstalled additional public root; compromised roots may need new binary. Existing healthy offline launches do not recheck root expiry.

http.status: explicit local-development service composition; production startup remains refused
http.control_routes: Same upload/validate/publish/promote/rollback/audit/outbox route suffixes, envelope names, scoped bearer RBAC, response fields, bounds and error codes as release-v1.http; signed_manifest and signed_assignment are strictly v2 types
http.updates: GET /v2/updates with the same complete scope/runtime/channel/installation query; 200 {signed_assignment,artifact_url}, 204 if no eligible v2 assignment. artifact_url always names /v2/artifacts/{digest}?organization=&project=
http.artifact: GET /v2/artifacts/{digest}?organization=&project= returns only published immutable v2 {signed_manifest,payload}; no admin credentials in public delivery
http.selection: Route version, signed schema/protocol, registered host protocol and exact scope/runtime authority must agree; never probe or fall back. Wrong-version public offers return204 and artifacts404; mutations reject
http.channels: Channel identity retains organization/project/app/environment/platform/runtime/channel. Publishing a new fingerprint does not replace older runtime heads. Same content rollback requires a fresh greater signed assignment sequence
http.idempotency_audit: Both versions share tenant-scoped idempotency, audit/outbox and transaction locking. Method plus versioned path plus exact body bind the request hash; cross-version reuse of the same key conflicts. Earlier successful response bytes and audit-chain hashes remain intact
http.local_storage: Existing schema1 snapshots remain readable. First successful durable v2 domain write atomically upgrades to schema2 with strict mutually exclusive typed record variants. Failed requests cannot upgrade. Older binaries refuse schema2; no downgrade conversion
http.postgres_storage: Existing opaque bytea signed records support both versions after strict schema dispatch and complete typed validation. No migration001 SQL, checksum or schema-version change; FORCE RLS, immutability and transaction semantics preserved
http.clients: Existing CLI publication and Go reference recovery remain v1. The bounded public Swift HTTP integration consumer verifies small TEST payloads and typed grants/limits; no production payload downloader, activation, guest capability execution, device OTA or hosted qualification is claimed
